                    text: [32m'# Search | Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-02-27, last updated: 2026-02-26, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/0.23.0/api/search.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|filter_by|no|Filter conditions for refining your search results.A field can be matched against one or more values.Examples:-\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense filter_by Syntax and Examples\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-30, last updated: 2026-08-07, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/tips-for-filtering.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense allows you to filter your search results based on the values of specific fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can\n'[39m +
                      [32m'use the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'filter_by\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'parameter to specify a custom filter string.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Note that the base format for a filter is\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'field: <operator> <value>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'. Every filter field must have\n'[39m +
                      [32m'a ** after it. :**- ✅ Correct:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can use an asterisk (\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m') to denote a prefix in a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'field filter. This allows you to filter for fields that **begin with** the provided prefix:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When filtering on fields inside nested array objects, you need to use a special syntax to ensure the filters are applied to the same object within the array. The syntax is:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'filter_by=ingredients.{name:=cheese && concentration:<50}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When filtering for joined collection, you use the'[39m
                  },

                    text: [32m'# Exact filter_by queries return results in unexpected order, numbers\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"drush sapi-ts 'sapi_ts_index' '*' 'field_vehicle_model__name' \\\n"[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Here's the query:\n"[39m +

                      [32m'?q=*\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Understanding `filter_by` Functionality in Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2025-11-03, [Read more](https://threads.typesense.org/t/understanding-filter-by-functionality-in-typesense/2K2e9c)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Kishore Nallan clarified that marking field as a facet isn't needed in 0.22.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A question regarding `filter_by` , from the docs > Filter conditions for refining your search results.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'> `country: USA` > > To match a string field exactly, you have to mark the field as a facet and use the := operator.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For eg: `category:= Shoe` will match documents from the category shoes and not from a category like `shoe rack`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This distinction is going away in 0.22.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You don't have to mark the field as facet anymore for exact filter.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'As for the semantics, without the `=` symbol, Typsense will do a contains check, so will find records containig the string `shoe` e.g. `running shoes` , `basketball shoes` etc.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'But with the `=`, it becomes a strict check, so only fields that has only the word `shoe` will be returned.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# exact match and phrase query supported? · Issue #272 · typesense/typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2021-05-19, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/issues/272)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"👋 @bnfd We don't support exact searching yet, but that's on our prioritized feature backlog.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'We do support the "-" operator which you can use to exclude specific words in the search query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Would something like\n'[39m +
                      [32m"` q: post.fireId, query_by: 'fireId', filter_by:`fireId:=${post.fireId}``\n"[39m +
                      [32m'work?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You would have to use `filter_by`:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'q=*, filter_by: fireId:=${post.fireId}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`q` and `query_by` are only for text based search queries that users type in.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For structured search where the exact value is already known programmatically, you want to use filter_by.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Search Curation API\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-30, last updated: 2026-08-07, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/30.2/api/curation.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### # Parameters\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Parameter|Required|Description|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|--|--|--|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|rule.query|One of either `rule.query` or `rule.filter_by` is required.|Indicates what search queries should be overridden.|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|rule.match|no|Indicates whether the match on the query term should be `exact` or `contains`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Required when `rule.query` is set.|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|rule.filter_by|One of either `rule.query` or `rule.filter_by` is required.|Indicates that the override should apply when the `filter_by` parameter in a search query *exactly* matches the string specified here (including backticks, spaces, brackets, etc).|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|filter_by|no|A filter by clause that is applied to any search query that matches the override rule.|'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Prefix Filtering Fails on Filter_By Solved\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-02-02, last updated: 2026-02-10, [Read more](https://www.technetexperts.com/typesense-prefix-filter-failure/amp/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To ensure reliable exact matching, prefix matching (‘*’), and boolean combination logic within ‘filter_by’, the fields must be explicitly optimized for structured filtering.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In Typesense, this is achieved by setting the ‘facet’ property to ‘true’.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Crucially, the ‘filter_by’ operation, especially when performing exact matches (‘:=’) or prefix searches (‘*’), needs access to the full, raw string value, independent of full-text search tokens.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Setting ‘facet: true’ instructs Typesense to build a separate, dedicated inverted index optimized specifically for filtering operations.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Create a new field, for example, ‘fl_adep_exact’, and ensure it is indexed as a non-searchable, non-tokenized field if possible (though Typesense strongly encourages ‘facet: true’ for this use case).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the original field is needed for relevance search, the query must be split: use the original field for the ‘q’ (query) parameter, and the new ‘_exact’ field for the ‘filter_by’ parameter.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The definitive solution is enabling ‘facet: true’ for any string fields required for structured filtering (‘*’, ‘:=’, range filtering).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Absolutely.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Boolean Search with Tags - Typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-30, last updated: 2026-07-14, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/boolean-tag-search.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense supports boolean queries like this when filtering, using the `filter_by` property.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'However, since the `filter_by` property only supports exact matches, unlike the `q` parameter which supports full-text search with typo tolerance, this can mean trading-off some of the flexibility of full-text search.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The data flow for a tag-based search interface is as follows:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. The user types a query into the search box.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. The query is sent to the Typesense server using `query_by` across all fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. The results are sorted by which field they match, and what the value of that field is.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'4. Tags are constructed from the sorted values and displayed to the user as a list.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'5. The user selects multiple tags to form a tag cloud.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'6. The tag cloud is used to generate a search request using a `filter_by` template.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'7. The search request is sent to the Typesense server using `multiSearch`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'8. The results are displayed to the user.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"For array fields like genres, we'll use the `:` operator, and for string fields like title, we'll use `:=` for exact matching."[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Search FAQs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-30, last updated: 2026-08-04, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/faqs.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### # Boolean Search using the filter_by search parameter:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you need to do more structured queries, then you can use the `filter_by` search parameter, which supports complex boolean expressions with precedence, etc.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"For eg, let's say we want to search for `software engineering lead` OR `software engineering manager` in the same search query.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'You could do something like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"q": "*",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"filter_by": "job_title:[software engineering lead, software engineering manager]"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"q": "*",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"filter_by": "job_title:software engineering lead && job_location:[remote, hybrid]"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"q": "*",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"filter_by": "job_title:=software*"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"q": "shoes",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"filter_by": "category:=Athletic",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"max_candidates": 100\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you click on say "John Denver" and want to only fetch songs where the artist is "John Denver", that is called filtering.'[39m
                  }
                ]

                    text: [32m'# Typesense filter_by Syntax and Examples\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-30, last updated: 2026-08-07, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/tips-for-filtering.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense allows you to filter your search results based on the values of specific fields.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can\n'[39m +
                      [32m'use the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Note that the base format for a filter is\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'field: <operator> <value>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When filtering on fields inside nested array objects, you need to use a special syntax to ensure the filters are applied to the same object within the array. The syntax is:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'filter_by=ingredients.{name:=cheese && concentration:<50}\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Search\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-02-27, last updated: 2026-02-26, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/0.23.0/api/search.html)\n'[39m +

                      [32m'|Parameter|Required|Description|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|filter_by|no|Filter conditions for refining your search results.A field can be matched against one or more values.Examples:-\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` country: [USA, UK] ``` returns documents that have\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` country ``` of\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` USA ``` OR\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` filter_by=author:!= JK Rowling ``` Numeric Filtering:Filter documents with numeric values between a min and max value, using the range operator\n'[39m +

                      [32m'``` > ``` ,\n'[39m +

                      [32m'``` < ``` ,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` <= ``` ,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` = ``` . Examples:-\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` num_employees:[10..100] ``` -\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` num_employees:<40 ``` Multiple Conditions:Separate multiple conditions with the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` && ``` operator.Examples:-\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` num_employees:>100 && country: [USA, UK] ``` -\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` categories:=Shoes && categories:=Outdoor ``` To do ORs acrossdifferent fields (eg: Color is blue OR category is Shoe), you want to split each condition into separate queries in a multi-query request and then aggregate the text match scores across requests.\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Filter by array length in typesense query\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Filter documents with numeric values between a min and max value, using the range operator [min..max] or using simple comparison operators >, >= <, <=, =.\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# What and how do I perform a search operation in ...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"'filter_by' : 'average_rating:>100',\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- sort_by: A list of numerical fields and sort orders that will be used to order your results.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'You can specify up to three sort fields.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'One or more values can be matched against a field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'-\n'[39m +

                      [32m'You must mark a field as a facet and use the := operator to match a string field exactly.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, genre:=ROMANTIC will return documents from the genre ROMANTIC rather than a genre like ROMANTIC COMEDY.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# ANTLR4 grammar for filter expression · Issue #396 · typesense/typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2021-10-03, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/issues/396)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense currently supports a simple `filter_by` syntax that can do ANDs between different fields, but does not support ORs between fields or compound filter conditions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Existing syntax\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Filtering a single value\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name: Steve Smith\n'[39m +
                      [32m'age: 10\n'[39m +
                      [32m'is_enabled: true\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Filtering multiple values of the same field (we do an OR)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'name: [Steve Smith, `Jack & Jill`]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'age: [10, 15]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Numerical comparators (we support <, >, <=, >= and ..)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'age:>10\n'[39m +
                      [32m'age: [>=10, 20]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'age:[10..100]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Exact equals (e.g. "shoes" in the example below will not match a field with the value "running shoes")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'category:= shoes\n'[39m +
                      [32m'category:= [`Running Shoes, Men`, Sneaker]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# ANDing multiple conditions\n'[39m +
                      [32m'age:>20 && category:= [`Running Shoes, Men`, Sneaker]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Example:\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Typesense Search API Parameters\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# What and how do I perform a search operation in Typesense? - DEV ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2022-05-04, last updated: 2025-09-13, [Read more](https://dev.to/aviyel/what-and-how-do-i-perform-a-search-operation-in-typesense-5gc5)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- filter_by: The "filter by" argument is used to refine your search results by filtering conditions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'One or more values can be matched against a field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'-\n'[39m +
                      [32m'genre: CRIME genre: [ROMANTIC, COMEDY].\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You must mark a field as a facet and use the := operator to match a string field exactly.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For example, genre:=ROMANTIC will return documents from the genre ROMANTIC rather than a genre like ROMANTIC COMEDY.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can also use multiple values to filter: genre:= [Romantic, Comedy].\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Using the range operator [min..max], you can get numeric values between a minimum and maximum value.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'For example, average_rating:>9 && genre: [ROMANTIC,DRAMA]'[39m

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# ANTLR4 grammar for filter expression · Issue #396 · typesense/typesense\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2021-10-03, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/issues/396)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Typesense currently supports a simple `filter_by` syntax that can do ANDs between different fields, but does not support ORs between fields or compound filter conditions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We want to support advance filtering operations and that requires generating a grammar for the existing filter syntax and extending it to support ORs (via `||`) and compound expressions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Numerical comparators (we support <, >, <=, >= and ..)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'age:>10\n'[39m +
                      [32m'age: [>=10, 20]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'age:[10..100]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'# Exact equals (e.g. "shoes" in the example below will not match a field with the value "running shoes")\n'[39m +
                      [32m'category:= shoes\n'[39m +
                      [32m'category:= [`Running Shoes, Men`, Sneaker]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'We now want to support compound filters and `||` (OR) conditions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Example:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'((age: <5 || age: >10) && category:= [shoes]) || is_curated: true\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# search: OR("||") operator support in filter_by clause #281 - GitHub\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2021-06-01, last updated: 2026-04-17, [Read more](https://github.com/typesense/typesense/issues/281)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`filter_by` currently only supports `OR`ing values in the same field, and `AND`ing values across fields or the same field.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you need to `OR` across fields, the work-around would be to send multiple queries using the `multi_search` endpoint, with each query having a particular field in the `filter_by` expression and then aggregating the results client-side for these queries.'[39m

                    text: [32m'# Typesense Search FAQs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-04, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/guide/faqs.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'#### # Boolean Search using the filter_by search parameter:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you need to do more structured queries, then you can use the `filter_by` search parameter, which supports complex boolean expressions with precedence, etc.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"For eg, let's say we want to search for `software engineering lead` OR `software engineering manager` in the same search query.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'You could do something like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"q": "*",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"filter_by": "job_title:[software engineering lead, software engineering manager]"\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Understanding `filter_by` Functionality in Typesense\n'[39m +

                  [32m"  if ('field' in node && 'cmp' in node && 'value' in node) {\n"[39m +

                  [32m'    const field = node.field;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    const cmp = node.cmp;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    const value = node.value;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    function escapeStr(val) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m"      if (typeof val !== 'string') {\n"[39m +
                  [32m'        val = String(val);\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      }\n'[39m +

When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel using the executeCommand tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:\n'[39m +

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how should we refactor the database schema"\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +

            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.
